title: Preservation of the invariant through a halting run
statement: Let a register program, its initial label, an oracle, a decider machine, and a starting-state assignment be fixed, together with natural numbers $B,W$, two configurations $c,c'$ on the same Boolean input, an output word $o$, and a bit $b$. Suppose the program simulates $c'$ from $c$ in finitely many steps, with no oracle-call state and all register heads between $-1$ and $W$ at every intermediate step. Also suppose that from $c'$ it reaches a halting configuration whose output is $o$ followed by $b$, whose register heads lie between $-1$ and $W$, and whose every earlier configuration satisfies the invariant. Then from $c$ it reaches a halting configuration with that same output and head bounds, and every earlier configuration satisfies the invariant.
hypotheses_covered: At each simulation step before the endpoint, no call state is active
At each such step, every register head position is between $-1$ and $W$
A run from $c'$ halts with output $o$ followed by $b$
Every register head position at that halting configuration is between $-1$ and $W$
Every earlier configuration in the run from $c'$ satisfies the invariant
